channel.title: Alignment Research Blog
channel.description: Informal updates from the OpenAI team.

item.title: Measuring Reward-Seeking by Instilling Contrastive Beliefs
item.dc:creator: Axel Højmark, Jérémy Scheurer, Jenny Nitishinskaya, Felix Hofstätter, Jason Wolfe, Theodore Ehrenborg, Bronson Schoen, Alexander Meinke
item.description: A new test for whether models change their behavior based on what they believe a grader rewards.

item.title: Reinforcement learning towards broadly and persistently beneficial models
item.dc:creator: Akshay V. Jagadeesh, Rahul Arora, Mikhail Trofimov, Khaled Saab, Ali Malik, Foivos Tsimpourlas, Karan Singhal
item.description: Training targeting beneficial behavior in realistic scenarios produces broad improvements in alignment that generalize across domains and persist under adversarial pressure.

item.title: Can public chat data predict real-world AI misalignments?
item.dc:creator: Hannah Sheahan and Micah Carroll
item.description: Bridging private deployment evidence and public AI evaluation

item.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
item.dc:creator: Micah Carroll, Tomek Korbak, Zehao Dou, Bowen Baker, Ian Kivlichan
item.description: We found limited accidental CoT grading in some released models, fixed the affected reward pathways, and found no clear evidence that monitorability degraded.

item.title: Auto-review of agent actions without synchronous human oversight
item.dc:creator: Maja Trębacz, Sam Arnesen, Ollie Matthews, Dylan Hurd, Won Park, Owen Lin, Joe Gershenson
item.description: Auto-review offers a safer default for deploying coding agents, using a separate agent to approve or deny boundary-crossing actions.

item.title: Open Sourcing Monitorability Evaluations
item.dc:creator: Author list TBD
item.description: We open-source datasets and code from our Monitoring Monitorability paper, and share a new filtering strategy for noise-dominated intervention evaluation instances.

item.title: Introducing the OpenAI Safety Fellowship
item.dc:creator: OpenAI
item.description: A pilot program to support independent safety and alignment research and develop the next generation of talent

item.title: How far does alignment midtraining generalize?
item.dc:creator: Tomek Korbak, Cameron Raymond, Micah Carroll, Marcus Williams, Mikita Balesni, Alan Guo, Jason Wolfe, Akshay Jagadeesh, Ian Kivlichan
item.description: Preliminary experiments on alignment and misalignment midtraining, reasoning posttraining, and generalization to chat and agentic evals.

item.title: Introducing Model Spec Evals
item.description: A new evaluation suite for measuring how well models follow the OpenAI Model Spec.

item.title: Training agents to self-report misbehavior
item.dc:creator: Bruce W. Lee, Yueh-Han Chen and Tomek Korbak
item.description: We train agents to call a reporting tool when they covertly misbehave, sharply reducing undetected attacks.

item.title: Interpreting Black Box Reward Models
item.dc:creator: Paloma Sodhi, Yueheng Li, Jessica Landon, Eric Wallace and Kai Chen
item.description: ARGO distills black-box reward models into interpretable rubrics using reinforcement learning.

item.title: Discovering unknown AI misalignments in real-world usage
item.dc:creator: Hannah Sheahan
item.description: Reasoning models can find and understand unknown misaligned behaviors from how users respond.

item.title: Why we are excited about confessions
item.dc:creator: Boaz Barak, Gabriel Wu, Jeremy Chen and Manas Joglekar
item.description: Deeper analysis of confession training and comparisons to chain-of-thought monitoring.

item.title: CoVal: Learning values-aware rubrics from the crowd
item.dc:creator: Zoë Hitzig, Mitchell Gordon, Tyna Eloundou, Adam Kalai and Sandhini Agarwal
item.description: An experimental dataset of crowd-written rubrics that surfaces why people prefer one model output over another.

item.title: Helpful assistant features suppress emergent misalignment
item.dc:creator: Tom Dupre la Tour, in collaboration with the Interpretability team
item.description: Emergent misalignment not only activates misaligned personas, but also suppresses helpful assistant personas.

item.title: Sidestepping Evaluation Awareness and Anticipating Misalignment with Production Evaluations
item.dc:creator: Marcus Williams, Cameron Raymond and Micah Carroll, in collaboration with the Safety Oversight team
item.description: A pipeline to uncover unknown misaligned behavior and scale the creation of realistic evaluations.

item.title: Debugging misaligned completions with sparse-autoencoder latent attribution
item.dc:creator: Tom Dupre la Tour and Dan Mossing, in collaboration with the Interpretability team
item.description: Efficiently finding features that cause behaviors.

item.title: A Practical Approach to Verifying Code at Scale
item.dc:creator: Maja Trębacz, Sam Arnesen, Albin Cassirer, Max Johnson, Xin Lin, Thibault Sottiaux, in collaboration with the rest of the Codex team
item.description: We train and deploy an AI review agent optimised for precision and real-world use, enabling oversight to scale with autonomous code generation.

item.title: Hello World
item.dc:creator: OpenAI
item.description: Introducing our blog on alignment research.
